name: Straightening hair brush
lead: A straightening hair brush is a heated paddle-style brush that straightens hair as the user brushes through it, combining the surface of a hairbrush with the heated plates of a flat iron. According to Wikipedia, a ceramic straightening brush was patented in 2013, and Sharon Rabi released the first one under the DAFNI brand in 2015 [1].

The tool has a larger heated surface than a traditional flat iron [1]. No published clinical studies of straightening brushes were found; the underlying heat-straightening mechanism is the same as for flat irons, which work by breaking hydrogen bonds in the hair cortex, with bonds able to re-form when hair is exposed to moisture, and which can cause damage when overused [1].

paras: The brush has bristles or teeth set on a heated ceramic surface so that hair is straightened as it is combed through, in place of clamping sections between plates [1].
No studies specific to straightening brushes were found. Wikipedia's general warning for heated hair tools is that overuse can cause severe hair damage [1].
No studies found. Heat straightening with flat irons has been examined in laboratory work, but no human trial of a straightening brush was identified.

timeline.event: Sharon Rabi releases the first straightening brush under the DAFNI brand [1]

card.summary: Heated paddle brush that straightens as you brush; same heat mechanism as a flat iron, with no dedicated research.
card.note: No studies specific to straightening brushes; general heat-damage cautions apply.

quick.overview:
A straightening brush is a heated paddle brush that straightens hair as it is brushed through, a hybrid of a hairbrush and a flat iron. The first brand-name version, DAFNI, was released in 2015 after a ceramic design was patented in 2013.

No dedicated studies of these brushes were found.
quick.mechanism: Heat reshapes hydrogen bonds in the hair so it can be held straight, as with a flat iron; the bonds can re-form with moisture.
quick.risks: Overuse of heated styling tools can cause severe hair damage, and hot surfaces can burn skin.
